To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) plasma triglycerides, in addition to cholesterol, are an important risk factor for MI in men; 2) triglycerides are a stronger risk factor for MI than cholesterol; 3) the rate of MI increases with both triglyceride and cholesterol levels, but the increase is more pronounced for triglycerides; 4) triglyceride and/or cholesterol values in the top quintile are found in 25-30% of men in the general population, i.e
age, blood BP, smoking and fasting plasma triglycerides are the four most important risk factors for MI.
elevated plasma triglycerides are an independent risk factor for MI and more important than elevated plasma cholesterol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the plasma lipids in relation to other known risk factors in a prospective study.
the role of plasma lipids as risk factors in a population of men with a low incidence of myocardial infarcts.
the importance of plasma triglyceride as a risk factor for MI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma triglycerides are as important as cholesterol as risk factors for MI.
both elevated plasma cholesterol and triglyceride are risk factors for MI in men, and that the triglyceride level is a more important risk factor than cholesterol.
plasma triglycerides, but not plasma cholesterol, is a risk factor for MI in young men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
elevated plasma triglyceride levels, particularly in combination with elevated plasma cholesterol levels, are associated with a substantially increased risk of myocardial infarct in middle-aged men.
plasma triglycerides are as important as, if not more important than, cholesterol as a risk factor for MI in middle-aged men.
the plasma triglyceride level is an independent risk factor for MI and that the triglyceride level may be a more important risk factor than cholesterol for MI in men below 60.
The main takeaway from our work is that
elevated plasma triglycerides are more important as a coronary risk factor than elevated cholesterol.
the plasma concentration of triglycerides is an independent risk factor for myocardial infraction and that the risk is higher when the concentration of triglyceride and cholesterol is high.
elevated plasma triglycerides are more closely associated with MI than cholesterol.
